subproblem.title: Countable bounded Borel cover with uniform lower Lipschitz constants from pointwise local lower bounds (parent Steps 2, 5–8)
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Euclidean norm |·| and Borel σ-algebra, and let F be a normed additive commutative group (F : Type with NormedAddCommGroup F) with norm |·|. Let f : ℝⁿ → F be continuous, and let R ⊆ ℝⁿ be a Borel set such that for every w ∈ R there is c > 0 with c·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ c. Then there are sets T_p ⊆ ℝⁿ (p ∈ ℕ) with R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p such that, for every p: T_p is a Borel set; T_p is bounded; T_p ⊆ R; and there is c > 0 with c·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ T_p.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) {F : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup F] (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → F) (R : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))), Continuous f → MeasurableSet R → (∀ w ∈ R, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ‖u‖ ≤ c → c * ‖u‖ ≤ ‖f (w + u) - f w‖) → ∃ T : ℕ → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), R ⊆ ⋃ p, T p ∧ ∀ p, MeasurableSet (T p) ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (T p) ∧ T p ⊆ R ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ v ∈ T p, ∀ w ∈ T p, c * ‖v - w‖ ≤ ‖f v - f w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. |·| denotes the norms of ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and of F. On ℝⁿ, dist(x, y) = |x − y|, and B_ρ(q) := {x ∈ ℝⁿ : |x − q| ≤ ρ} is the closed ball. For k ∈ ℕ put r_k := 1/(k+1) ∈ (0, 1] and
   G_k := ⋂_{u ∈ ℝⁿ, |u| ≤ r_k} {w ∈ ℝⁿ : r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|}.
Thus w ∈ G_k if and only if r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)| for every u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ r_k. (These are the sets G_k of the parent proof; here R is an arbitrary Borel set with the stated pointwise property.)

1. (G_k is closed, hence Borel.) Fix k and u ∈ ℝⁿ. The map w ↦ |f(w + u) − f(w)| is continuous, because f is continuous and translation w ↦ w + u, subtraction and the norm are continuous. The map w ↦ r_k·|u| is constant. Hence {w : r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|} is closed (Mathlib isClosed_le). An intersection of closed sets is closed (isClosed_biInter), so G_k is closed and therefore Borel (IsClosed.measurableSet).

2. (Every point of R lies in some G_k.) Let w ∈ R, and let c > 0 be given by the hypothesis for w. By the Archimedean property (Mathlib exists_nat_one_div_lt) there is k ∈ ℕ with r_k = 1/(k+1) < c. Let u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ r_k. Then |u| ≤ c, so the hypothesis gives c·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|. Also r_k·|u| ≤ c·|u|, because r_k ≤ c and |u| ≥ 0. Hence r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|, and since u was arbitrary, w ∈ G_k.

3. (Small balls.) ℝⁿ is separable and nonempty (it contains 0), so there is a sequence (q_m)_{m∈ℕ} in ℝⁿ with dense range (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.exists_dense_seq). Let w ∈ ℝⁿ and k ∈ ℕ. Density, applied with the radius r_k/2 > 0 (DenseRange.exists_dist_lt), gives m ∈ ℕ with dist(w, q_m) < r_k/2, so w ∈ B_{r_k/2}(q_m).

4. (The family.) For p ∈ ℕ, let (k(p), m(p)) := Nat.unpair p and define
   T_p := R ∩ G_{k(p)} ∩ B_{r_{k(p)}/2}(q_{m(p)}).

5. (Covering.) Let w ∈ R. By step 2 there is k with w ∈ G_k, and by step 3 there is m with w ∈ B_{r_k/2}(q_m). Put p := Nat.pair k m. Then Nat.unpair p = (k, m) (Nat.unpair_pair), so T_p = R ∩ G_k ∩ B_{r_k/2}(q_m) contains w. Hence R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p.

6. (Properties of each T_p.) Fix p and write k := k(p), m := m(p).
 (a) T_p is Borel. R is Borel by hypothesis, G_k is Borel by step 1, and the closed ball B_{r_k/2}(q_m) is Borel (measurableSet_closedBall). A finite intersection of Borel sets is Borel.
 (b) T_p is bounded. It is contained in the closed ball B_{r_k/2}(q_m), which is bounded (Metric.isBounded_closedBall, Bornology.IsBounded.subset).
 (c) T_p ⊆ R by definition.
 (d) Put c := r_k = 1/(k+1) > 0, and let v, w ∈ T_p. Both lie in B_{r_k/2}(q_m), so |v − w| = dist(v, w) ≤ dist(v, q_m) + dist(w, q_m) ≤ r_k/2 + r_k/2 = r_k (dist_triangle_right). Let u := v − w; then |u| ≤ r_k and w + u = v. Since w ∈ G_k, the defining inequality of G_k for this u gives r_k·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|, that is, c·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)|.

Steps 5 and 6 are exactly the assertions. R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p, and each T_p is Borel, bounded and contained in R. Each T_p also satisfies the lower bound with the constant c = 1/(k(p)+1) > 0.
proof_key_steps: G_k := ⋂_{|u| ≤ r_k} {w : r_k|u| ≤ |f(w+u) − f(w)|} with r_k = 1/(k+1) is closed because f is continuous (isClosed_le, isClosed_biInter), hence Borel
For w ∈ R with pointwise constant c, choosing k with 1/(k+1) < c (exists_nat_one_div_lt) gives w ∈ G_k
A dense sequence (q_m) (TopologicalSpace.exists_dense_seq) gives, for each k, closed balls B_{r_k/2}(q_m) covering ℝⁿ (DenseRange.exists_dist_lt)
T_p := R ∩ G_k ∩ B_{r_k/2}(q_m), with (k, m) = Nat.unpair p, covers R (Nat.unpair_pair); each T_p is Borel, bounded and contained in R
For v, w ∈ T_p one has |v − w| ≤ r_k, so taking u := v − w in the definition of G_k gives r_k|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)|

audit.reason: The standalone one-line proposition exactly matches the continuity, Borel-set, and pointwise-bound hypotheses and every conclusion. Continuity makes G_k closed; choosing r_k < c covers R; dense half-radius balls and Nat.pair give the bounded Borel cover. The diameter estimate and u = v − w prove the uniform lower bound. The proof is complete and independent of the first child, so its empty dependency list is correct. Applying it with the first child's bounds and the pinned regular-set measurability theorem yields the exact selected parent.

subproblem.title: Local lower bound at a point of differentiability with injective derivative (parent Steps 3–4)
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Euclidean norm |·|, and let F be a real normed vector space (F : Type with NormedAddCommGroup F and NormedSpace ℝ F) with norm |·|. Let f : ℝⁿ → F and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose f is (Fréchet) differentiable at w and its derivative Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w : ℝⁿ → F is injective. Then there exists c > 0 such that c·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)| for every u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ c.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) {F : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → F) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)), DifferentiableAt ℝ f w → Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ f w) → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ u : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), ‖u‖ ≤ c → c * ‖u‖ ≤ ‖f (w + u) - f w‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. |·| denotes the norms of ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) and of F, and dist(u, 0) = |u|. Put L := Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w, a continuous ℝ-linear map ℝⁿ → F; by hypothesis L is injective. (This is Steps 3–4 of the parent proof, with the radius and the lower-bound constant merged into one number c.)

1. (Lower bound for the injective linear map L.) Because L is injective, its underlying linear map has trivial kernel (Mathlib LinearMap.ker_eq_bot). Since ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional, Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith gives K ∈ ℝ≥0 with K > 0 such that L is K-anti-Lipschitz. ZeroHomClass.bound_of_antilipschitz turns this into |u| ≤ K·|Lu| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ. [Direct argument: if n = 0, every u equals 0 and any K > 0 works. If n ≥ 1, the unit sphere of ℝⁿ is compact and nonempty, and e ↦ |Le| is continuous and, by injectivity, strictly positive on it. So it attains a minimum μ > 0, and K := 1/μ works by homogeneity of the norms and linearity of L.] Put m := K⁻¹ > 0. Multiplying |u| ≤ K·|Lu| by m > 0 and using m·K = 1 gives
   (1) m·|u| ≤ |Lu| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ.

2. (Differentiability as a little-o estimate.) Since f is differentiable at w, it has Fréchet derivative L at w (DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt). By Mathlib hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero, this means that u ↦ f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu is o(u) as u → 0. Applying the definition of o(·) with the positive constant m/2 (Asymptotics.IsLittleO.def) shows that |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu| ≤ (m/2)·|u| for all u in a neighbourhood of 0. By Metric.eventually_nhds_iff there is r > 0 such that
   (2) |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu| ≤ (m/2)·|u| for all u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| = dist(u, 0) < r.

3. (Lower bound for increments near w.) Let u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| < r. Since Lu = (f(w + u) − f(w)) − (f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu), the triangle inequality (norm_sub_le together with sub_sub_cancel) gives |Lu| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)| + |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu|. Combining this with (1) and (2):
   (3) |f(w + u) − f(w)| ≥ |Lu| − |f(w + u) − f(w) − Lu| ≥ m·|u| − (m/2)·|u| = (m/2)·|u|.

4. (Choice of c.) Put c := min(m/2, r/2). Then c > 0 because m > 0 and r > 0. Let u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ c. Then |u| ≤ r/2 < r, so (3) applies. Since c ≤ m/2 and |u| ≥ 0, we get c·|u| ≤ (m/2)·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)|. Thus c > 0 and c·|u| ≤ |f(w + u) − f(w)| for every u ∈ ℝⁿ with |u| ≤ c, which is the assertion.
proof_key_steps: Injectivity of L = fderiv ℝ f w on finite-dimensional ℝⁿ gives K > 0 with |u| ≤ K|Lu| (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith with LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, then ZeroHomClass.bound_of_antilipschitz); with m := 1/K > 0 this gives m|u| ≤ |Lu| for all u
Differentiability at w (hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero, Asymptotics.IsLittleO.def with constant m/2, Metric.eventually_nhds_iff) gives r > 0 with |f(w+u) − f(w) − Lu| ≤ (m/2)|u| for |u| < r
Triangle inequality: |f(w+u) − f(w)| ≥ |Lu| − |f(w+u) − f(w) − Lu| ≥ (m/2)|u| for |u| < r
With c := min(m/2, r/2) > 0, every u with |u| ≤ c has |u| < r, so c|u| ≤ (m/2)|u| ≤ |f(w+u) − f(w)|

audit.reason: The standalone one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and all hypotheses. Injectivity supplies a positive linear lower bound, including when n = 0. Differentiability supplies the little-o estimate; the triangle inequality and c = min(m/2, r/2) establish the precise closed-radius conclusion. The arbitrary normed target needs no completeness assumption. Every step is supplied, non-circular, and sufficient for formalization; the empty dependency list is correct.
